deep.reconstruction: Context: in E477 Euler studies the double series S(m,n) = Σ_{k≥1} k^{-m} (1 + 2^{-n} + … + k^{-n}) = Σ_{k≥j≥1} k^{-m} j^{-n}. This is the non-strict ('star') double zeta value, ζ*(m,n) = ζ(m,n) + ζ(m+n), where ζ(m,n) = Σ_{k>j} k^{-m} j^{-n}. On the previous page he showed that multiplying the two series and splitting the terms into k>j, k<j and k=j gives P + Q = ζ(m)ζ(n) + ζ(m+n), with P = S(m,n) and Q = S(n,m). In modern terms this is the stuffle (harmonic-product) relation. This page finishes that sentence: the values ζ(2k) are known in terms of π ('per peripheriam circuli'), and odd values are only known numerically ('summae vero proximae'). In §3 he sets m = n, so P = Q, which gives S(n,n) = ½ζ(n)² + ½ζ(2n). He introduces the letters Δ = ζ(1) (divergent), A = ζ(2), B = ζ(3), C = ζ(4), D = ζ(5), E = ζ(6), …, I = ζ(10). He then lists the cases n = 1,…,5: S(1,1) = ½Δ² + ½A, S(2,2) = ½A² + ½C, S(3,3) = ½B² + ½E, S(4,4) = ½C² + ½G, S(5,5) = ½D² + ½I. On the next page he remarks that the first is infinite. Equivalently, the strict values are ζ(n,n) = (ζ(n)² − ζ(2n))/2. This is the symmetric-function identity e₂ = (p₁² − p₂)/2. The purpose is to obtain closed-form evaluations of the double series, which is the paper's goal.
errors: No mathematical errors on this page. The n = 1 line is formally divergent on both sides; Euler acknowledges this on the next page ('primae seriei summam Δ esse infinitam').

ideas.what: Evaluation of the symmetric double sum Σ_{k≥j} 1/(k^n j^n) = ½(ζ(n)² + ζ(2n))
ideas.modern_name: Symmetric (star) double zeta value ζ*(n,n); the stuffle relation in the diagonal case; Newton's identity e₂ = (p₁² − p₂)/2 applied to power sums
ideas.where_published: E477 itself; the Euler–Goldbach letters of 1742; discussed in modern MZV literature (e.g. Borwein–Bradley–Broadhurst; Sandifer's columns)

ideas.what: Sum of the two swapped double series equals ζ(m)ζ(n) + ζ(m+n)
ideas.modern_name: Stuffle / harmonic shuffle product of multiple zeta values (depth 2)

ideas.modern_name: Euler's evaluation of ζ(2k); the open status of odd zeta values
